title: LinkedIn Company Workforce & Profile Intelligence Input

companyUrls.title: Company URLs
companyUrls.description: LinkedIn company, showcase or school URLs — or bare slugs. All of these work: 'microsoft', 'linkedin.com/company/microsoft', 'https://www.linkedin.com/company/microsoft/about/'. Duplicates and locale subdomains are collapsed to one row.

outputMode.title: Output Mode
outputMode.description: Default: one row per declared office, with the company's identity repeated on each row and the address broken into city / region / postal code / country — Microsoft yields 45 rows. Switch to 'One row per company' for a single profile row per input URL instead.

sessionCookie.title: LinkedIn Session Cookie (li_at)
sessionCookie.description: ⚠️ Required only for the country breakdown. LinkedIn shows a company's top-5 employee locations publicly and gates everything beyond that behind a login, so a full per-country breakdown needs an authenticated session. Paste the value of the 'li_at' cookie from a logged-in LinkedIn session. Every other field in the output works without it. Use a secondary account: automated requests can get an account restricted.

includeCountryBreakdown.title: Employee Count by Country
includeCountryBreakdown.description: The headline feature: employee headcount per country, beyond LinkedIn's default top-5 display. Needs the session cookie above. This costs one authenticated request per country, so it is by far the slowest part of a run — see 'Country scan' below to bound it.

includeLocationEmployeeCounts.title: Count Employees per Location
includeLocationEmployeeCounts.description: ⚠️ SLOW. Adds a metro-level headcount to every campus row, on top of the country sweep. Needs the session cookie and Output Mode = one row per location. Costs roughly one extra authenticated request per office, so Microsoft's 45 campuses add ~45 requests (~90 seconds) to that company alone. Without it, each campus still carries its country's headcount at no extra cost.

includeLocations.title: Declared Office Locations
includeLocations.description: Every office location the company lists on its page, not just the HQ. Compare against the country breakdown to see where a company says it operates versus where its staff actually are.

includeSpecialties.title: Specialties
includeSpecialties.description: Self-declared specialty and focus tags from the About panel.

includeAffiliatedCompanies.title: Affiliated Companies
includeAffiliatedCompanies.description: Subsidiary, regional, showcase and acquired pages linked from this company's page.

includeSimilarCompanies.title: Similar Companies
includeSimilarCompanies.description: LinkedIn's own 'similar pages' / 'people also viewed' suggestions. Useful for building a competitor set from one seed company.

includeRecentUpdates.title: Recent Posts
includeRecentUpdates.description: Recent posts from the page's activity feed, with date and engagement counts.

includeFeaturedEmployees.title: Featured Employees
includeFeaturedEmployees.description: The small sample of employee profiles LinkedIn surfaces publicly. This is a sample LinkedIn chose to show, not a roster — the country breakdown is the workforce signal.

countries.title: Countries to Scan
countries.description: Restrict the country sweep to these countries. Leave empty to sweep a built-in list of 125 countries ordered by LinkedIn membership. Setting this is the single most effective way to cut run time when you already know which markets you care about.

countryScanCoveragePercent.title: Stop After Coverage (%)
countryScanCoveragePercent.description: Stop sweeping once this percentage of the company's total LinkedIn headcount has been placed in a country. Below 100 on purpose: members who list no location are in the total but in no country bucket, so a 100% bar would always walk the full list.

maxCountriesScanned.title: Max Countries Per Company
maxCountriesScanned.description: Hard ceiling on countries queried per company, regardless of coverage. Bounds worst-case run time.

maxAuthenticatedRequests.title: Authenticated Request Budget
maxAuthenticatedRequests.description: Hard cap on authenticated LinkedIn requests for the whole run. Once spent, remaining companies are returned with public fields only rather than pushing the account further. Leave empty for no cap.

requestDelayMs.title: Delay Between Authenticated Requests (ms)
requestDelayMs.description: Spacing between authenticated LinkedIn requests, jittered ±20%. 1500–2000ms is the safe band; lowering it raises the chance of a rate-limit or an account restriction. Applies to the authenticated lane only — public pages are governed by concurrency.

verifyWebsite.title: Verify Website Domain
verifyWebsite.description: Check whether the listed website's domain still resolves in DNS, and report it as websiteStatus. A dead domain on a live LinkedIn page is a real signal — acquired, folded, or rebranded. Costs one DNS lookup per company, no HTTP request.

cacheTtlDays.title: Cache TTL (days)
cacheTtlDays.description: Reuse a stored row for a company scraped within this many days instead of re-fetching it. Firmographics and country distribution change slowly, so this mostly saves authenticated request budget. Set to 0 to always re-scrape.

proxyConfiguration.title: Proxy Configuration
proxyConfiguration.description: Residential proxies are strongly recommended, and close to mandatory when a session cookie is used: authenticated LinkedIn traffic from a datacenter IP is a strong anomaly signal. The authenticated lane pins one sticky proxy session for the whole run and never rotates inside it.

maxConcurrency.title: Max Concurrency (public pages)
maxConcurrency.description: Requests in flight for the public-page phase. Does not affect the authenticated lane, which is always serialised.

maxRequestRetries.title: Max Request Retries
maxRequestRetries.description: How many times to retry a blocked or failed public page before giving up and returning the row with success: false.
